_fixture.source: hand-made contract fixture (feat/technique spec section 6); no /api/technique backend recorded yet
_fixture.what: GET /api/technique/sessions/df149ca2d149/balance shape, on the recorded Suzuka session the car setup fixtures use (its stored setup: front ARB 15, front wing 10, diff on throttle 90, rear ARB 10, rear suspension 10). Symptoms and suggestions are hand-made sample values; the rear suspension's 'already at its minimum' is invented to exercise a blocked suggestion.

symptoms.text: Mid-corner understeer at T2 and T7 (medium speed) on 3 of 3 laps, including your best lap this session: at the limit the front tyres ran 6.4° more slip angle than the rears (heuristic threshold 3°).
symptoms.text_simple: The car pushed wide in the middle of T2 and T7 on 3 of 3 laps, even on your best lap.

symptoms.text: Exit oversteer at T11 (slow) on 3 of 3 laps, including your best lap this session, with wheelspin on 2 of them: the rear tyres ran 1.6° more slip angle than the fronts (heuristic threshold 1°).
symptoms.text_simple: The rear stepped out leaving T11 on 3 of 3 laps, even on your best lap.

symptoms.text: Entry understeer at T9 on laps 1 and 2 but not on your best lap (lap 3): that points at how the corner was driven (entry speed or line) more than the car.
symptoms.text_simple: The car pushed wide into T9 on 2 of 3 laps, but not on your best lap: that is more about how the corner was driven than the car.

suggestions.label: Front Anti-Roll Bar
suggestions.effect: A softer front bar gives more front grip in slow and medium corners, at the cost of slower response and more body roll.
suggestions.why: A softer front bar lets the front tyres take more load in slow and medium corners, where this car pushed wide.
suggestions.hypothesis: Front Anti-Roll Bar 15 -> 13: The car pushed wide in the middle of T2 and T7 on 3 of 3 laps, even on your best lap. Expected: A softer front bar gives more front grip in slow and medium corners, at the cost of slower response and more body roll.

suggestions.label: Front Wing Aero
suggestions.effect: More front downforce gives sharper turn-in and more front grip in medium and fast corners. The cost is drag (lower top speed), and if the front wing is high compared with the rear the rear gets light and oversteery.
suggestions.why: More front wing adds front grip in medium and fast corners.
suggestions.hypothesis: Front Wing Aero 10 -> 12: The car pushed wide in the middle of T2 and T7 on 3 of 3 laps, even on your best lap. Expected: More front downforce gives sharper turn-in and more front grip in medium and fast corners. The cost is drag (lower top speed), and if the front wing is high compared with the rear the rear gets light and oversteery.

suggestions.label: Differential Adjustment On Throttle
suggestions.effect: The diff is more open under power, so the car is calmer and less likely to spin on exits. The cost is drive, because the inside wheel can spin up, and very low values can also make it push wide.
suggestions.why: A more open differential under power calms the rear on the way out of slow corners.
suggestions.hypothesis: Differential Adjustment On Throttle 90 -> 80: The rear stepped out leaving T11 on 3 of 3 laps, even on your best lap. Expected: The diff is more open under power, so the car is calmer and less likely to spin on exits. The cost is drive, because the inside wheel can spin up, and very low values can also make it push wide.

suggestions.label: Rear Anti-Roll Bar
suggestions.effect: A softer rear bar gives more rear grip and traction and a calmer exit, but less rotation, so there is more understeer.
suggestions.why: A softer rear bar gives the rear more grip on exits.
suggestions.hypothesis: Rear Anti-Roll Bar 10 -> 8: The rear stepped out leaving T11 on 3 of 3 laps, even on your best lap. Expected: A softer rear bar gives more rear grip and traction and a calmer exit, but less rotation, so there is more understeer.

suggestions.label: Rear Suspension
suggestions.effect: A softer rear gives better traction and a calmer rear out of slow corners and over kerbs. The car feels lazier and may understeer, and too soft risks bottoming out.
suggestions.why: A softer rear gives better traction out of slow corners.
suggestions.hypothesis: Rear Suspension 1 -> 1: The rear stepped out leaving T11 on 3 of 3 laps, even on your best lap. Expected: A softer rear gives better traction and a calmer rear out of slow corners and over kerbs. The car feels lazier and may understeer, and too soft risks bottoming out.
suggestions.blocked: Rear Suspension is already at its minimum (1) for the 2025 car.

setup.caveat: A setup is a starting point, not a guaranteed fix: rule out technique first (braking point, entry speed, brake release, throttle), then change one thing at a time and compare laps.
setup.note: Rear Anti-Roll Bar is suggested lower for the exit oversteer only; no other symptom wants it changed.

balance.note: Thresholds are heuristics, tested on recorded laps.

notes: Braking assist is on (medium): the game adds its own braking, so these brake figures are not all yours.
ABS on: the game prevents lock-ups, so they are not analysed.
